_comment: Fragment 50 — D-96: three Judge rulings. Sprint gates phase, the POC is original scope, Q11 gets a design direction. Merged 2026-08-22.

nodes.label: D-96 — Three Judge Rulings
nodes.description: The Judge ruled on all three items Lane A escalated: S0 incompleteness blocks Phase 1, the POC commercial flow is original project scope rather than new, and Q11 needs a design direction from Lane A rather than a further escalation.
nodes.rationale: Two of the three rulings correct Lane A rather than Lane B. Escalating a question is not the same as having framed it correctly, and one escalation carried a mischaracterisation inside it.

nodes.label: A Phase Cannot Close While the Sprint It Enables Is Incomplete
nodes.description: Condition 5 of phase closure. The thirteen unimplemented config rows reported by config-coupling stop being a background residual and become a named closure blocker for Phase 1.
nodes.rationale: A real question rather than a formality. Phases and sprints are different scopes, and D-94 used exactly that reasoning to call the build spec unaffected. The ruling closes it in the other direction.

nodes.label: Closing Phase 1 Requires Work Only Lane B May Do
nodes.description: Phase 2 was never validly opened, so Lane B cannot implement the outstanding config rows without acting outside an opened phase. Closing Phase 1 requires work only Lane B may do, and Lane B may not act until Phase 1 closes.
nodes.rationale: Stated rather than engineered away. Three exits exist and the way out is a Judge decision about scope, not a Lane A decision about paths. Lane A implementing the rows is rejected outright: that is a crossing into the application surface and the reason the lane model exists.

nodes.label: The POC Commercial Flow Is Original Scope, Not New
nodes.description: Stripe shipped in package.json from scaffolding and was removed during S0. The removal is evidence the flow existed, not evidence it never did. The no-monetization exclusion is a simplification for the current stage, practical rather than permanent.
nodes.rationale: Lane A had been reading a scoping decision as a denial of existence. The source says not now and Lane A heard not real, which is a conflict asserted past what the source says in its second recorded instance.

nodes.label: One Engine, Two Flows, One Sellable Item
nodes.description: The MVP and the POC are two flows of one editorial brief. The POC sells exactly one item, publicly-expandable content with a report, entering at the trigger and traversing the same phase gates. The elaborate cart, payment-provider, drain, account-claiming model is not adopted.
nodes.rationale: The simplification of what is sold had never actually been performed, and this ruling performs it. It is a narrowing rather than an expansion, and it holds the standing invariant that the pipeline is never forked.

nodes.label: Q11 — a Boolean Cannot Exclude Logged Overrides
nodes.description: Two shapes were specified. A boolean crossing flag is what the sprint plan selects by default if nobody decides; a three-value status column matches the functional requirement. Lane A recommends the status column.
nodes.rationale: The metric excludes logged overrides, which requires telling not-applicable and override-not-four-eyes apart, and a boolean maps both to false. Under the boolean shape the metric cannot be computed from its own declared data source. A crossing boolean, if wanted, is a derived view and never a stored duplicate.

nodes.label: The Draft Is the Earlier Event
nodes.description: Deferred past S1 and must resolve before the migration draft cannot both govern one sequence. S0 creates only the hold location, no draft exists before the field shape and the whole S1 window settle, and moving the approved draft into the apply set is the S1 authorization act.
nodes.rationale: Irreversibility begins when a field name is committed to text an executor will apply, which is earlier than the sprint that applies it.
